# Motion workshop

Open `index.html` through the game host at `/game/animation-expansion/player/`. This is a functioning 2D animatic reviewer, not a finished film. It selects isolated, exact source-text beats for all 24 chapters from `../story/story_manifest.json` and defaults to chapter 2 and its proposed cinematic backdrop when delivered, leaving the other session’s workshop opening coverage independent. A fallback reads `../../engine2/world.json` if the production manifest is absent. It never concatenates all branch alternatives into an alleged linear screenplay. Source strings retain punctuation and line breaks. The transcript panel exposes source pointer, record ID and SHA256, and links the runtime snapshot where applicable.

The canonical view animates existing game crew walking frames, entrance/exit, timed anticipation/strike/recovery transforms and creature sprite changes against the source floor plan. It is staging, not recorded gameplay. The optional concept continuity test uses six existing flattened portrait assets, neutral/eyes-closed for three proposed identities; it deliberately assigns none to canonical names. Expression swaps and camera/breathing transforms are not articulated rigs or lip-sync. Only two existing scenery plates are copied. Assets originated in the concurrent session’s `animation_pack`, copied as an immutable snapshot with `assets/source-manifest.json` and actual copy hashes in `assets/copied-assets.json`. The other session may update its source assets independently; validation uses this package’s copy hashes. Game crew/monster/terrain sheets are referenced from `../../engine2/art/` rather than duplicated. Chapter 1 uses civilian Sable art and does not invent a recruited companion on narrator/Sable beats.

A generated action-study view supports `../motion/crew-actions-v1.png` and `../motion/monster-actions-v1.png` as 6-column, 3-row atlases at 8 fps. Crew rows are Iona, Rook and Mira; secondary crew rows in `crew-actions-secondary-v1.png` are Brass, Riven and Veyr; monster rows are beetle, moth and raven. These are generated action drafts with continuity review still required. Matching named crew source beats can use the new atlas in attack mode. A cinematic scenery view supports the 2×2 `../motion/scenery-chapters-2-5.png` atlas as proposed viaduct, well, chapel and archive plates for chapters 2–5. Missing optional assets display a delivery-pending notice, with canonical map playback still working. Reload the page after optional art arrives.

Controls include chapter and beat selectors, view and action selectors, pause, restart, previous/next, timeline scrubbing, loop, and JSON beat export. The player is dependency-free and makes no network requests outside its own relative files. Serve the complete game tree rather than opening `file://` because browsers restrict JSON fetches. `validate_player.py` checks source record coverage, copied-asset hashes, JavaScript syntax and required controls; it does not substitute for browser visual review or claim device FPS.

## Credit-free voiced animation pass 2.6

Builds separate timelines for all 1,500 source records. The default menu shows 170 beats with exact recordings; all 399 recordings are reachable, spanning chapters 1–24. Narration and blocked/unrecorded lines remain silent. Captions and canonical sprite selection follow the current audio cue; audio currentTime drives the clock, and pauses/seeks cancel the prior player. Alternate outcomes remain separate records. Interface receipts are optional and never spoken. An 11.546-second repair-bench MP4 was rendered locally at 1280x720/24fps with timed subtitles and existing sprite cutouts; its reproducible renderer lives at development/render_voiced_animatic.py. This is limited 2D staging/breathing and existing frame animation, not fully rigged anatomy or phoneme lip sync.

Validation: 58 Node checks passed, including complete timeline-to-voice matching. Browser confirmed Rook-to-Sable subtitle/speaker transition against playback and zero remaining audio elements after Pause. The rendered MP4 fully decodes. No new service generation was used.
